from __future__ import annotations
import csv
from collections import Counter
from pathlib import Path
import pandas as pd
from source_io import fetch

SOURCE_URL = ('https://data.dft.gov.uk/road-accidents-safety-data/'
              'dft-road-casualty-statistics-collision-last-5-years.csv')
YEARS = (2021, 2022, 2023, 2024, 2025)
REQUIRED = ['collision_index', 'collision_year', 'police_force', 'collision_severity',
            'date', 'time', 'day_of_week', 'local_authority_ons_district',
            'first_road_class', 'road_type', 'speed_limit', 'light_conditions',
            'weather_conditions', 'road_surface_conditions',
            'special_conditions_at_site', 'urban_or_rural_area', 'trunk_road_flag']
FEATURES = ['speed_limit', 'light_conditions', 'weather_conditions',
            'road_surface_conditions', 'special_conditions_at_site',
            'first_road_class', 'road_type', 'urban_or_rural_area',
            'trunk_road_flag', 'police_force', 'local_authority_ons_district',
            'hour_of_day', 'day_of_week', 'month']
NUMERIC_FEATURES = ['speed_limit', 'light_conditions', 'weather_conditions',
                    'road_surface_conditions', 'special_conditions_at_site',
                    'first_road_class', 'road_type', 'urban_or_rural_area',
                    'trunk_road_flag', 'police_force']
COLUMNS = ['collision_index', 'collision_datetime'] + FEATURES + ['target']


def _as_int(series):
    value = pd.to_numeric(series, errors='coerce')
    value = value.mask(value < 0)
    return value.round().astype('Int64')


def _header(path):
    with open(path, 'r', encoding='utf-8-sig', newline='') as handle:
        return [cell.strip() for cell in next(csv.reader(handle))]


def _write_csv(frame, path):
    path = Path(path)
    path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    frame.to_csv(path, index=False, lineterminator=chr(10), na_rep='')


def build(output: Path, cache: Path):
    output = Path(output)
    cache = Path(cache)
    output.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    cache.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    checks = []

    def record(name, observed, expected, passed, kind=None):
        item = {'check': name, 'observed': str(observed),
                'expected': str(expected), 'passed': bool(passed)}
        if kind is not None:
            item['kind'] = kind
        checks.append(item)
        if not passed:
            raise AssertionError(name + ': observed=' + str(observed) + ' expected=' + str(expected))

    local = Path(fetch(SOURCE_URL, cache, 'stats19_collision_last_5_years.csv'))
    size_mb = local.stat().st_size / (1024.0 * 1024.0)
    record('five-year collision bundle size matches publisher description',
           f'{size_mb:.1f} MB',
           'publisher lists 97.7 MB for the last-five-years collision CSV (allow >50 MB)',
           size_mb > 50.0)

    header = _header(local)
    lower_to_original = {}
    for name in header:
        lower_to_original.setdefault(name.lower(), name)
    missing = [name for name in REQUIRED if name not in lower_to_original]
    record('source header exposes the required collision fields',
           f'{len(header)} columns; missing={missing}',
           f'all required fields present: {REQUIRED}',
           not missing)

    usecols = [lower_to_original[name] for name in REQUIRED]
    rename = {lower_to_original[name]: name for name in REQUIRED}
    reader = pd.read_csv(local, dtype=str, keep_default_na=False, na_filter=False,
                         usecols=usecols, chunksize=50000, encoding='utf-8-sig')

    parts = []
    total_rows = 0
    year_rows = 0
    year_counts = Counter()
    date_fail = 0
    time_fail = 0
    parse_fail_rows = 0
    dow_mismatch = 0
    missing_severity = 0
    bad_severity = 0
    id_missing = 0
    severity_values = set()
    dow_values = set()
    examples = []

    for raw in reader:
        total_rows += len(raw)
        raw = raw.rename(columns=rename)
        for name in REQUIRED:
            raw[name] = raw[name].astype(str).str.strip()
        year_int = _as_int(raw['collision_year'])
        for value, count in year_int.dropna().value_counts().items():
            year_counts[int(value)] += int(count)
        in_years = year_int.isin(list(YEARS))
        raw = raw.loc[in_years].copy()
        if raw.empty:
            continue
        year_rows += len(raw)
        if len(examples) < 3:
            examples.extend((raw['date'] + ' ' + raw['time']).head(3).tolist())

        date_text = raw['date']
        parsed_date = pd.to_datetime(date_text, format='%d/%m/%Y', errors='coerce')
        bad_date = parsed_date.isna() & date_text.ne('')
        if bad_date.any():
            parsed_date.loc[bad_date] = pd.to_datetime(
                date_text.loc[bad_date], dayfirst=True, errors='coerce')

        time_parts = raw['time'].str.split(':', expand=True)
        for col in range(time_parts.shape[1], 3):
            time_parts[col] = pd.NA
        hour = pd.to_numeric(time_parts[0], errors='coerce')
        minute = pd.to_numeric(time_parts[1], errors='coerce')
        second_numeric = pd.to_numeric(time_parts[2], errors='coerce')
        second_ok = time_parts[2].isna() | second_numeric.between(0, 59)
        second = second_numeric.fillna(0)
        time_ok = hour.between(0, 23) & minute.between(0, 59) & second_ok
        if time_parts.shape[1] > 3:
            time_ok = time_ok & False
        total_seconds = hour * 3600 + minute * 60 + second
        stamp = parsed_date + pd.to_timedelta(total_seconds, unit='s')
        stamp = stamp.where(parsed_date.notna() & time_ok)

        date_fail += int(parsed_date.isna().sum())
        time_fail += int((~time_ok).sum())
        parse_fail_rows += int((parsed_date.isna() | (~time_ok)).sum())

        day_of_week = _as_int(raw['day_of_week'])
        expected_dow = (((stamp.dt.dayofweek + 1) % 7) + 1).round().astype('Int64')
        dow_mismatch += int((day_of_week.notna() & expected_dow.notna() &
                             (day_of_week != expected_dow)).sum())
        dow_values.update(int(value) for value in day_of_week.dropna().unique())

        severity = _as_int(raw['collision_severity'])
        missing_severity += int(severity.isna().sum())
        nonnull_severity = severity.dropna()
        severity_values.update(int(value) for value in nonnull_severity.unique())
        bad_severity += int((~nonnull_severity.isin([1, 2, 3])).sum())

        id_missing += int(raw['collision_index'].eq('').sum())
        keep = (stamp.notna() & severity.isin([1, 2, 3]) &
                raw['collision_index'].ne(''))
        raw = raw.loc[keep].copy()
        if raw.empty:
            continue
        stamp = stamp.loc[keep]
        severity = severity.loc[keep]
        day_of_week = day_of_week.loc[keep]

        frame = pd.DataFrame(index=raw.index)
        frame['collision_index'] = raw['collision_index']
        frame['collision_datetime'] = stamp.dt.strftime('%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S')
        for name in NUMERIC_FEATURES:
            frame[name] = _as_int(raw[name])
        frame['local_authority_ons_district'] = raw['local_authority_ons_district'].replace(
            {'': pd.NA, '-1': pd.NA})
        frame['hour_of_day'] = stamp.dt.hour.astype('Int64')
        frame['day_of_week'] = day_of_week.astype('Int64')
        frame['month'] = stamp.dt.month.astype('Int64')
        frame['target'] = severity.isin([1, 2]).astype('int8')
        parts.append(frame)

    if not parts:
        raise AssertionError('no eligible collision rows found')
    combined = pd.concat(parts, ignore_index=True)

    observed_years = sorted(year for year in year_counts if year in YEARS)
    counts = {year: year_counts[year] for year in observed_years}
    record('fixed collision years 2021-2025 are present',
           f'years={observed_years}; counts={counts}',
           'all five fixed years present: 2021, 2022, 2023, 2024, 2025',
           observed_years == list(YEARS))
    record('five-year bundle has the expected row scale',
           f'total_rows={total_rows}; selected_year_rows={year_rows}',
           'publisher describes roughly 95,000-110,000 collisions per year; at least 400,000 across 2021-2025',
           total_rows > 400000 and year_rows > 400000)
    parse_rate = 1.0 - (parse_fail_rows / year_rows) if year_rows else 0.0
    record('collision date and time parse under DfT DD/MM/YYYY and HH:MM frames',
           f'examples={examples}; date_failures={date_fail}; time_failures={time_fail}; parse_rate={parse_rate:.6f}',
           'date DD/MM/YYYY and 24-hour HH:MM; at least 99.99% parseable, invalid rows excluded',
           parse_rate >= 0.9999, kind='unit')
    record('collision_severity uses documented DfT codes',
           f'values={sorted(severity_values)}; missing={missing_severity}; out_of_domain={bad_severity}',
           '1=Fatal, 2=Serious, 3=Slight; non-missing values all in {1,2,3}; missing/out-of-range excluded',
           severity_values == {1, 2, 3} and bad_severity == 0, kind='unit')
    record('day_of_week follows DfT calendar coding',
           f'values={sorted(dow_values)}; mismatches={dow_mismatch}',
           '1=Sunday, 2=Monday, ..., 7=Saturday and must match the date',
           set(dow_values) <= {1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7} and len(dow_values) == 7 and dow_mismatch == 0,
           kind='unit')
    record('collision_index is present on every selected row',
           f'missing_ids={id_missing}',
           '0 missing stable collision identifiers',
           id_missing == 0)

    source_dups = int(combined.duplicated('collision_index').sum())
    if source_dups:
        combined = combined.drop_duplicates('collision_index', keep='first').reset_index(drop=True)
    output_dups = int(combined.duplicated('collision_index').sum())
    record('collision_index is unique after de-duplication',
           f'source_duplicate_rows={source_dups}; output_duplicate_ids={output_dups}',
           'one row per collision; 0 output duplicate ids',
           output_dups == 0)

    speed = combined['speed_limit'].dropna().astype(int)
    valid_limits = {20, 30, 40, 50, 60, 70, 99}
    nonstandard = int((~speed.isin(valid_limits)).sum())
    standard_fraction = float(speed.isin(valid_limits).mean()) if len(speed) else 0.0
    min_speed = int(speed.min()) if len(speed) else None
    max_speed = int(speed.max()) if len(speed) else None
    record('speed_limit is a posted road limit recorded in mph',
           f'n={len(speed)}; min={min_speed}; max={max_speed}; nonstandard={nonstandard}; standard_fraction={standard_fraction:.6f}',
           'DfT: 20/30/40/50/60/70 are the valid public-highway limits; 99=self-reported unknown; -1 missing is left blank; unit is mph',
           len(speed) > 0 and min_speed >= 0 and max_speed <= 99 and standard_fraction >= 0.999,
           kind='unit')

    target_values = sorted(int(value) for value in combined['target'].unique())
    positive_count = int(combined['target'].sum())
    record('target is a binary KSI indicator',
           f'values={target_values}; positives={positive_count}; rows={len(combined)}',
           '0/1 only; 1 for severity 1 or 2, 0 for severity 3',
           set(target_values) <= {0, 1}, kind='unit')
    missing_features = {name: int(combined[name].isna().sum()) for name in NUMERIC_FEATURES}
    negative_present = {name: int((combined[name].dropna() < 0).sum()) for name in NUMERIC_FEATURES}
    record('missing feature codes are not imputed as zero',
           f'negative_sentinels_remaining={negative_present}; missing_counts={missing_features}',
           'no negative sentinel remains; missing cells are blank, never zero-filled',
           all(value == 0 for value in negative_present.values()))
    record('shipped columns contain only declared ids, time, features and target',
           str(COLUMNS),
           'exactly the declared column list',
           list(combined.columns) == COLUMNS)
    forbidden = {'collision_severity', 'number_of_casualties', 'number_of_vehicles',
                 'enhanced_severity_collision', 'enhanced_collision_severity',
                 'collision_injury_based', 'collision_adjusted_severity_serious',
                 'collision_adjusted_severity_slight'}
    present = sorted(set(COLUMNS) & forbidden)
    record('no label source or post-outcome field is shipped as an input',
           f'forbidden_present={present}',
           'no severity, casualty-count, vehicle-count or adjusted-severity columns',
           not present)

    stamps = pd.to_datetime(combined['collision_datetime'], format='%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S', errors='coerce')
    record('shipped event timestamps parse',
           f'null_timestamps={int(stamps.isna().sum())}',
           '0 null timestamps',
           int(stamps.isna().sum()) == 0)
    train_mask = ((stamps >= pd.Timestamp('2021-01-01T00:00:00')) &
                  (stamps < pd.Timestamp('2024-01-01T00:00:00')))
    eval_mask = ((stamps >= pd.Timestamp('2024-01-01T00:00:00')) &
                 (stamps < pd.Timestamp('2025-01-01T00:00:00')))
    holdout_mask = ((stamps >= pd.Timestamp('2025-01-01T00:00:00')) &
                    (stamps < pd.Timestamp('2026-01-01T00:00:00')))
    assigned = train_mask.astype(int) + eval_mask.astype(int) + holdout_mask.astype(int)
    unassigned = int((assigned == 0).sum())
    record('rows fall into exactly one fixed half-open split window',
           f'train={int(train_mask.sum())}; eval={int(eval_mask.sum())}; holdout={int(holdout_mask.sum())}; unassigned={unassigned}',
           'train [2021-01-01, 2024-01-01), eval [2024-01-01, 2025-01-01), holdout [2025-01-01, 2026-01-01)',
           unassigned == 0 and int(train_mask.sum()) > 0 and int(eval_mask.sum()) > 0 and int(holdout_mask.sum()) > 0)

    train = combined.loc[train_mask].sort_values(
        ['collision_datetime', 'collision_index'], kind='mergesort').reset_index(drop=True)
    eval_frame = combined.loc[eval_mask].sort_values(
        ['collision_datetime', 'collision_index'], kind='mergesort').reset_index(drop=True)
    holdout = combined.loc[holdout_mask].sort_values(
        ['collision_datetime', 'collision_index'], kind='mergesort').reset_index(drop=True)

    id_sets = [set(train['collision_index']), set(eval_frame['collision_index']),
               set(holdout['collision_index'])]
    overlaps = len(id_sets[0] & id_sets[1]) + len(id_sets[0] & id_sets[2]) + len(id_sets[1] & id_sets[2])
    record('split id sets are disjoint',
           f'overlap_ids={overlaps}',
           '0 overlapping ids',
           overlaps == 0)

    for label, frame in [('train', train), ('eval', eval_frame), ('holdout', holdout)]:
        values = sorted(int(value) for value in frame['target'].unique())
        positive_count = int(frame['target'].sum())
        record('split target is binary and nonempty: ' + label,
               f'rows={len(frame)}; positives={positive_count}; values={values}',
               'both 0 and 1 present; binary only',
               len(frame) > 0 and values == [0, 1])

    _write_csv(train.loc[:, COLUMNS], output / 'public' / 'train.csv')
    _write_csv(eval_frame.loc[:, COLUMNS], output / 'public' / 'eval.csv')
    _write_csv(holdout.loc[:, COLUMNS], output / 'private' / 'holdout.csv')
    written = [output / 'public' / 'train.csv', output / 'public' / 'eval.csv',
               output / 'private' / 'holdout.csv']
    record('three CSV artifacts are nonempty',
           f'sizes={[path.stat().st_size for path in written]}',
           'all > 0 bytes',
           all(path.stat().st_size > 0 for path in written))
    return checks
construction.construction_notes: Downloaded the DfT last-five-years collision CSV with fetch and streamed it in 50,000-row chunks, selecting only the declared fields. Dates are parsed as DD/MM/YYYY and times as 24-hour HH:MM; hour_of_day, month and collision_datetime are derived. collision_severity 1 or 2 maps to target 1 and 3 maps to 0; missing or out-of-domain severity is dropped, never imputed. Numeric feature sentinels at -1 are converted to blank nullable integers, so missing is not zero. collision_index is the stable event key, checked unique after de-duplication, and splits are the fixed half-open windows train 2021-2023, eval 2024, holdout 2025. Source checks assert the published header, year coverage, row scale, date/time frames, severity code frame, day-of-week coding, collision_index uniqueness, speed_limit mph frame, absence of label/post-outcome columns, and split integrity. No model metrics, training, qualification or packaging are performed. references.persistence_column is null because this file has no genuinely prior persistence score for a collision; enhanced and adjusted severity fields are concurrent outcome-derived fields and are excluded. No threshold is tuned and the holdout is never used for feature, target, threshold or split choice.

assumptions: Field semantics are taken from the DfT 2025 data guide and the stats19 schema; availability of the same fields at the collision-time prediction instant during 2021-2025 is assumed because only the current final annual snapshot is shipped.
The 2025 final annual release date is the publication anchor; exact publication dates for 2021-2024 are not asserted.
Police severity-recording practice changes by force and year; police_force is included as a recording-practice control, not as a causal risk factor.

cross_row_audit.auxiliary_files_review: Only the three declared CSV outputs are shipped; no fixture labels, answer scaffolds or auxiliary evaluation files.
cross_row_audit.rationale: All features are same-row road-environment and timing attributes; no lagged, rolling, cumulative or cross-collision construction.

collision_datetime.availability: derived from the published date and time fields; prediction-time historical availability assumed from the stable STATS19 specification

collision_index.availability: stable unique collision key present in the published collision file

day_of_week.availability: published source field using DfT coding 1=Sunday to 7=Saturday

first_road_class.availability: static road classification recorded on the collision return; prediction-time historical availability assumed

hour_of_day.availability: derived from the collision time field, not a separate source column

light_conditions.availability: same-row lighting condition at the collision; prediction-time historical availability assumed

local_authority_ons_district.availability: same-row ONS district code; prediction-time historical availability assumed

month.availability: derived from the collision date field, not a separate source column

police_force.availability: same-row police-force code; retained as a recording-practice control; prediction-time historical availability assumed

road_surface_conditions.availability: same-row road-surface state at the collision; prediction-time historical availability assumed

road_type.availability: static road layout recorded on the collision return; prediction-time historical availability assumed

special_conditions_at_site.availability: same-row site condition at the collision; prediction-time historical availability assumed

speed_limit.availability: same-row posted-limit field recorded at the collision; prediction-time historical availability assumed from the published STATS19 specification

trunk_road_flag.availability: static strategic-network flag recorded on the collision return; prediction-time historical availability assumed

urban_or_rural_area.availability: static area classification recorded on the collision return; prediction-time historical availability assumed

weather_conditions.availability: same-row weather condition at the collision; prediction-time historical availability assumed

limitations: Severity is partly a recording artefact: police forces adopted injury-based severity reporting at different times and slight-injury collisions are under-reported, so part of any signal from police_force, time-of-day or district may reflect recording practice rather than injury risk.

Predicting severity conditional on a collision having been reported is not the same as predicting collision risk; there is no exposure denominator such as traffic volume or vehicle kilometres in this file.

The open files omit contributory factors and other sensitive fields, which are the most informative pre-outcome variables and are available only to approved researchers, so the feature set is deliberately environment-and-timing only.

The 2024 STATS19 specification changed several variables; junction_detail, junction_control and pedestrian_crossing are excluded here for cross-year comparability, and remaining code sets should be checked year-by-year against the data guide before modelling.
Vehicle-level attributes live in a separate vehicle table joined on collision_index and are out of scope for this single-file release.
2021 is a COVID-distorted traffic year; if drift diagnostics show a break, the frozen fallback is to move the training window to 2022-2023 and keep eval 2024 and holdout 2025.
The bundle is re-issued annually, so construction pins the current vintage and records file checksums through fetch to keep the split reproducible.

selection.evidence: Every shipped feature is a same-row STATS19 attribute recorded on the collision return; collision_severity and all adjusted/enhanced severity fields are excluded from inputs.

vintage.evidence: Current final annual STATS19 files updated 30 July 2026; historical field availability is assumed, not proven.

measurements.frame: STATS19 collision date in DD/MM/YYYY and 24-hour HH:MM, combined as a local wall-clock timestamp
posted speed limit at the collision location
clock hour derived from the collision time field
DfT day code on the collision record
calendar month derived from the collision date
final published collision severity code used only to construct the target

task.decision_user: A road safety analyst or police collision-recording supervisor deciding which reported collisions to flag for specialist investigation and which road-environment configurations to prioritise for engineering treatment.
task.outcome_horizon: Final recorded severity for that collision in the published annual STATS19 record; severity may be revised after the event where injury-based reporting is used.
task.population: All collisions in the DfT collision extract with collision_year in 2021-2025, a valid date and time, and a non-missing collision_severity code in 1, 2 or 3. Eligibility uses only fields present on the record itself.
task.prediction_time: At the collision, using only road-environment and timing fields recorded on the STATS19 collision return; no casualty-severity, casualty-count or vehicle-count field.
task.question: Given a personal-injury collision already reported to police in Great Britain, will at least one person involved be killed or seriously injured (KSI), rather than only slightly injured?
task.simple_references: Majority class Slight; calendar-only model using month, day of week and hour; identity-only model using police force and district frequency encoding; single-variable rule speed_limit >= 50 mph.
task.split_policy: Fixed chronological boundaries: train 2021-01-01 to 2023-12-31, eval 2024-01-01 to 2024-12-31, holdout 2025-01-01 to 2025-12-31, represented as half-open instants. No embargo because every feature is same-row and contemporaneous.
task.target: collision_severity 1 Fatal or 2 Serious -> 1; collision_severity 3 Slight -> 0. Missing or out-of-range severity is excluded, never imputed.
task.usefulness: The label is a casualty-severity assessment made after the event, while inputs are road environment and timing known at the scene, so the task requires combination of speed limit, lighting, rurality, road class and time rather than copying a field.

features.note: Final annual STATS19 files are released in late July following the reference year; 2025 final was published 2026-07-30. Earlier release dates are not asserted.

observations.published: annual final release; exact date not captured
annual final release; exact date not captured

prediction_instant.citation: DfT final annual STATS19 release; 2025 final published 2026-07-30, with earlier years on the same annual cadence

construction.access_recipe: Download the bundled file https://data.dft.gov.uk/road-accidents-safety-data/dft-road-casualty-statistics-collision-last-5-years.csv (97.7 MB) with a plain HTTPS GET, or the per-year files (collision-2021.csv ... collision-2025.csv). Read with pandas.read_csv(dtype=str, keep_default_na=False) so codes such as -1 and '99' are not coerced; parse 'date' with format='%d/%m/%Y' and 'time' as HH:MM, then build hour/month; cast collision_severity to int and map {1,2}->1, {3}->0. Select only the whitelisted columns, drop every '*_historic' duplicate and every adjusted/enhanced severity field. Assert per-year row counts and the presence of collision_year values {2021..2025} and fail loudly otherwise; de-duplicate on collision_index.
construction.expected_size: Five-year bundle is 97.7 MB CSV; roughly 95,000-110,000 collisions per year, so approximately 500,000 rows for 2021-2025, with about 44 columns in the collision table. Documented observed examples: 106,004 rows and 44 columns for 2022; 104,258 rows and 38 columns for 2023 in the rOpenSci vignette. Well within a single modest worker.
construction.format: CSV, comma separated, one row per collision, coded integer values, no header quoting complications; date as DD/MM/YYYY and time as HH:MM per the data guide.
construction.source_examples: Header contains collision_index, collision_year, collision_ref_no, police_force, collision_severity, number_of_vehicles, number_of_casualties, date, day_of_week, time, local_authority_ons_district, first_road_class, road_type, speed_limit, light_conditions, weather_conditions, road_surface_conditions, special_conditions_at_site, urban_or_rural_area, did_police_officer_attend_scene_of_accident, trunk_road_flag, enhanced_collision_severity, collision_injury_based, collision_adjusted_severity_serious, collision_adjusted_severity_slight. Value checks from the DfT guide: collision_severity 1=Fatal, 2=Serious, 3=Slight; day_of_week 1=Sunday, 2=Monday, ...; enhanced_collision_severity uses 1/3/5/6/7 plus -1 for missing. Post-load checks: exactly three distinct collision_severity values, no nulls in date/time, and class balance near 75/25 slight vs KSI.

evidence.claim: Publisher page describing the record-level collision/vehicle/casualty files and stating only non-sensitive fields are published.
evidence.quote: Record level files providing data on personal injury road collisions in Great Britain from 1979, the vehicles involved and the consequential casualties.

evidence.claim: Open files exclude sensitive fields such as contributory factors, which are only available on request.

limitations: Severity is partly a recording artefact: police forces adopted injury-based severity reporting at different times and slight-injury collisions are under-reported, so part of any 'signal' from police_force, time-of-day or district may reflect recording practice rather than injury risk. DfT publishes severity-adjustment variables, but they are derived from the outcome measurement and are therefore excluded from inputs.
Predicting severity conditional on a collision having been reported is not the same as predicting collision risk; there is no exposure denominator (traffic volume, vehicle kilometres) in this file.

The open files omit contributory factors and other sensitive fields, which are the most informative pre-outcome variables and are available only to approved researchers, so the feature set is deliberately environment-and-timing only.

The 2024 STATS19 specification changed several variables; junction_detail, junction_control and pedestrian_crossing are excluded here for cross-year comparability, and remaining code sets should be checked year-by-year against the data guide before modelling.

Vehicle-level attributes (vehicle type, manoeuvre) live in a separate vehicle table joined on collision_index and are out of scope for the first single-file release; adding them is an extension, not part of this frozen task.
2021 is a COVID-distorted traffic year; if drift diagnostics show a break, the frozen fallback is to move the training window to 2022-2023 and keep eval 2024 / holdout 2025.
The bundle is re-issued annually, so construction must pin the vintage (30 July 2026 update) and record file checksums to keep the frozen split reproducible.
source.reason: The DfT STATS19 open collision extract is a single directly downloadable CSV (no account, no form, 19-20 MB per year, 97.7 MB for the bundled five-year file) with a published code list, an explicit UK Open Government Licence v3.0 that permits redistribution, no personal identifiers in the open fields, and one row per reported personal-injury collision in Great Britain. Because the prediction target is a post-assessment severity outcome while the candidate inputs are road-environment and timing descriptors recorded for the same collision, chronological year splits are clean and no cross-row or lagged feature is needed; no other source checked (Toronto permits, Chicago permits) combined this level of field documentation, licensing clarity and label cleanliness at comparable download cost.

task.outcome_horizon: Final recorded severity for that collision in the STATS19 record (severity may be revised after the event where injury-based reporting is used; the label is the severity in the published final annual file).
task.population: All collisions in the DfT collision extract with collision_year in 2021-2025, a valid date and time, and a non-missing collision_severity code in {1,2,3}. Eligibility uses only fields present on the record itself; no filtering on downstream outcome, on casualty rows, or on the presence of other rows. Restriction to 2021-2025 is fixed before any modelling and is driven by the publication vintage, not by observed performance.
task.prediction_time: At the moment the collision circumstances are recorded at/after the scene and before casualty severity has been finalised; every input is a property of the road environment or of the timing of the collision, none is an injury assessment.
task.question: Given a personal-injury collision already reported to police in Great Britain, will at least one person involved be killed or seriously injured (KSI), rather than slightly injured?
task.simple_references: Majority class (predict Slight for every collision, ~75% accuracy, AUC 0.5); calendar-only model (month, day of week, hour); identity/geography-only model (police force and local authority district frequency encoding); single-variable rule speed_limit >= 50 mph. These are the controls the release must be compared against before any claim of signal.
task.split_policy: Fixed chronological boundaries: train 2021-01-01 to 2023-12-31, eval 2024-01-01 to 2024-12-31, holdout 2025-01-01 to 2025-12-31. No embargo is required because every feature is same-row and contemporaneous (no lagged, rolling, cumulative or cross-collision features); the split is asserted disjoint at the date level and each collision appears exactly once (key = collision_index, cross-checked with collision_year + collision_ref_no). Boundaries are frozen before any metric is computed.
task.target: collision_severity == 1 (Fatal) or 2 (Serious) -> 1; collision_severity == 3 (Slight) -> 0. Rows with missing or out-of-range severity are dropped, never imputed.
task.usefulness: The label is a casualty-severity assessment made after the event, while the inputs are the road environment and timing known at the scene, so the task is not a field copy: a model must combine speed limit, lighting, rurality, road class and time-of-day to beat a strong ~75% 'all slight' majority. It has an operational reading (which reported collisions warrant specialist investigation) and an engineering reading (which environment configurations are associated with severe outcomes), and it is deliberately harder than models that are allowed to use casualty counts or vehicle counts.

source.title: Will a reported road collision in Great Britain involve a killed or seriously injured casualty? Predicting collision severity from road environment and timing at the scene
